programDefinitions.name: Foundation Barbell 5×5
programDefinitions.description: Three sessions a week, two alternating workouts, one rule: finish every set of five and the bar gets heavier next time. The simplest way to build a base of strength.
prerequisites: Can perform the five basic barbell lifts with an empty bar

programDefinitions.name: Double Progression Builder
programDefinitions.description: Every exercise owns a rep range. Fill the range on every set and the load goes up; until then the load waits while your reps climb. Four days, upper/lower.
prerequisites: Around six months of consistent training

programDefinitions.name: Tiered Stage Ladder
programDefinitions.description: Three tiers of work. When a heavy tier stalls, you do not deload — you trade reps for sets and keep the bar moving through three stages before resetting lighter.
prerequisites: Finished a linear progression program
Knows an approximate 5-rep max on the main lifts

programDefinitions.name: Heavy-Light-Medium 5×5
programDefinitions.description: One heavy day, one light day, one medium day that ends with a single top triple. Beat Friday's triple and the whole next week moves up 2.5 percent.
prerequisites: Session-to-session progression has stalled
Knows current 5-rep maxes
programDefinitions.notes: Success on the Medium day top triple is what 'weekCompleted' verifies for each *-top exposure; failing it marks the exposure failed for the week.

programDefinitions.name: Percent Cycle 4-Week
programDefinitions.description: Four-week waves of fives, threes, and heavy singles against a conservative training max. The last main set of each day is open-ended — rep records drive the next cycle.
prerequisites: About a year of training
A known or estimable one-rep max on the four main lifts

mainDayTemplate.comment: Each block week w and lift L expands to: main percents below of trainingMax(L), then first-set-last 5×5 at the week's first percent, then assistance.

programDefinitions.expansionNote: Weeks 1-3 are authored as transformations of week 0; the seed importer materializes all four weeks explicitly per block before validation, and the block repeats three times (12 weeks total).

programDefinitions.name: Wave Builder
programDefinitions.description: Two six-week phases built from three-week waves. Volume climbs in the base phase, intensity in the peak. The rep-record set at the end of each wave sets the next wave's weights.
prerequisites: Comfortable with percentage training and true rep-record sets
programDefinitions.expansionNote: The importer materializes each day from dayLayout, attaching the wave template to the main/developmental exercise ($self = the exercise's own exposure, $main = its mainRef). Waves advance via state, so the six template weeks per phase are identical; the wave index selects the week shape.

programDefinitions.name: RPE Bridge Block
programDefinitions.description: Learn to drive training by how heavy the bar actually feels. Work to one honest top set at a target effort, take percentage back-offs from it, and let the app suggest starting weights from your ratings.
prerequisites: About a year of training
Willing to rate every hard set on the RPE scale

sessionTemplates.topAndBackoff: top set: 1×N @ target RPE with load manual, min/max = 0.8–0.9 × e1RM($self); then 3 deferred back-off sets ×5 at 92.5% of the completed top set (generatesAfterSourceCompletion).

programDefinitions.name: Undulating Upper/Lower
programDefinitions.description: Each big lift appears twice a week wearing different hats: one heavy strength exposure, one higher-rep volume exposure. Each exposure keeps its own weights and progresses on its own rules.
prerequisites: A year or more of training

programDefinitions.name: Six-Week Block Strength
programDefinitions.description: Six weeks from volume to a platform-ready max: two weeks of muscular conditioning, a strength week, a heavy acclimation week, a peak week of near-max singles, then a taper and test day.
prerequisites: Confident technique on squat, bench, and deadlift
Known one-rep maxes

programDefinitions.name: Bench Press Specialization Matrix
warnings: Advanced program: bench press four times per week at high volume.
Requires an established pressing base, good recovery, and an honest current max.
All other heavy pressing is removed for the duration.
Do not run back-to-back; take at least a full training block between attempts.
programDefinitions.description: Three weeks, twelve sessions, one lift. Every workout is precomputed from your entered max, and each week adds a small fixed amount on top of the percentages. Finish, rest, and test.
prerequisites: Two or more years of training
Pain-free pressing
A current, honest bench press max

intakeInputs.hint: Use a real, recent max — not a goal

programDefinitions.name: Bodyweight Ladder Foundations
programDefinitions.description: Progress by earning harder exercises, not by adding plates. Each movement slot climbs a ladder of variations: own the rep range with clean form and the app offers you the next rung.

programDefinitions.name: Accumulation Wave Upper/Lower
programDefinitions.description: Hold the weight, add a set each week. When you complete the full five-set week, the wave converts into a heavier bar and the set count resets. Three waves, then an easy week.
prerequisites: Six or more months of training

programDefinitions.name: Velocity-Calibrated Strength
warnings: Experimental: designed around bar-speed readings from any velocity device or app, entered manually.
Works without a device — velocity rules simply stay silent and the percentage plan carries you.
programDefinitions.description: Let bar speed set the day's weights. A standard warm-up single tells the app how you're moving today; main work stays inside a target speed zone and stops before grinding.
prerequisites: Consistent technique on the main lifts
A velocity device or app is recommended

structure: Warm-up ramp singles at 45% / 60% / 75% of 1RM; the 75% single is the readiness probe (velocity logged, progressionEligible false except probe evaluation).
Main: 4×3 at 80% of 1RM, targetMeanVelocity zone 0.50–0.70 m/s, velocityLossStopPercent 20.

programDefinitions.name: Powerlifting Double-Exposure Practice
programDefinitions.description: A four-week synthetic conformance program with separately keyed competition, tempo, pause, and close-grip exposures. It is an original GymTracker engine fixture, not an official federation or coach program.
prerequisites: Known one-repetition maximums for squat, bench press, and deadlift
Consistent technique on the prescribed variations
warnings: Percentages are prescriptions, not automatic readiness or safety decisions.

provenance.statement: Original GymTracker prescription created to prove repeated exercise occurrences, independent exposure keys, percentage prescriptions, and restart lifecycle behavior.

programDefinitions.name: SkiErg 1,000 m Progression
programDefinitions.description: Concept2's six-week, twice-weekly progression toward a 1,000 m SkiErg test. Complete a separate 500 m benchmark before starting and use that recorded pace to guide the intervals.
prerequisites: Complete a 500 m SkiErg time trial before starting and record the result as your benchmark pace.
warnings: Schedule the two SkiErg sessions on non-consecutive days and keep other training appropriate to your experience and recovery.

provenance.statement: The scheduled distances, set counts, rest intervals, frequency, benchmark instruction, and final 1,000 m test reproduce Concept2's publicly available 2017 SkiErg World Sprints training format. GymTracker supplies only execution and history mechanics.

programDefinitions.name: Weightlifting Complex to Competition
programDefinitions.description: An original eight-week, three-session progression from technical shared-load complexes toward competition-lift practice and a three-attempt Snatch and Clean & Jerk test.
prerequisites: Consistent Snatch and Clean & Jerk technique under qualified coaching.
Known training maxes for Snatch, Clean & Jerk, Front Squat, and Back Squat.
Ability to record each complex component outcome honestly before completing its parent attempt.
warnings: This advanced practice plan is not individualized coaching; stop an attempt when technique cannot be maintained.
The three-miss rule creates an advisory decision and never stops work automatically.

provenance.statement: GymTracker authored every session and percentage in this original adaptation. Public sources support the move from preparatory complexes toward competition specificity and the final two-lift, three-attempt test format; they do not provide this eight-week prescription.

programDefinitions.name: Conjugate Rotation Wave
programDefinitions.description: A six-week original GymTracker adaptation of the max-effort / dynamic-effort conjugate method: a rotating max-effort exercise for squat and bench pattern each week, paired with fixed dynamic-effort speed work against compensatory-acceleration percentages. Each max-effort session is a ramp of three to five progressively heavier singles -- no more than three attempts above ninety percent -- stopping at a clean technical single, followed by three sets of three at eighty-five percent of that single.
prerequisites: At least one year of consistent barbell squat, bench, and deadlift training
Comfortable performing a single-repetition max-effort attempt with a spotter or safety arms
Known one-repetition maximums for Box Squat, Back Squat, Deadlift, and Bench Press
warnings: Max-effort work is autoregulated -- stop the ramp at a clean technical single, not a grinding or form-breaking rep.
Percentages are prescriptions, not automatic readiness or safety decisions.

provenance.statement: GymTracker authored every weekly exercise rotation, percentage, set, and repetition scheme in this six-week adaptation. Public strength-and-conditioning literature supports only the general max-effort/dynamic-effort conjugate method concept -- rotating near-maximal single-repetition work with submaximal speed work against compensatory-acceleration percentages -- not this program's specific schedule, exercise selection, or numbers. This is not presented as Westside Barbell's or any other organization's official program.

programDefinitions.name: Strongman Contest Preparation
programDefinitions.description: A six-week original GymTracker strongman contest-preparation adaptation. Two base weeks build load tolerance on log press, farmer's hold, deadlift, yoke, sandbag loading and farmer's carry; two build weeks raise intensity and add a deadlift ladder, a sandbag medley and bag-toss practice; a simulation week rehearses a contest-style event sequence; a final week cuts volume in half at sixty to seventy percent loads for a technical assessment.
prerequisites: Prior experience with strongman implements (log, yoke, farmer's handles, sandbag) under coached supervision
Known one-repetition or best-effort maximums for log press, farmer's hold, deadlift, yoke carry, and farmer's carry
warnings: Every farmer's-hold and farmer's-carry percentage is a per-hand load, never a combined total -- do not compare it to a total-load lift.
Strongman implements vary between gyms and competitions; treat the prescribed percentages as a starting point and adjust to the equipment actually available.
Percentages are prescriptions, not automatic readiness or safety decisions.

provenance.statement: GymTracker authored every weekly load, set, repetition, distance, and duration in this six-week adaptation. Public strength-sport literature supports only the general contest-preparation shape -- base loading, an intensity build, a full event-simulation rehearsal, and a reduced-volume taper into a technical check -- not this program's specific numbers. This is not presented as any federation's, gym's, or coach's official program.

programDefinitions.name: Fitness Racing Base to Peak
programDefinitions.description: An eight-week original GymTracker adaptation for hybrid fitness-racing events: an aerobic base run, strength work, running intervals, station skill paired with compromised running, and a weekly race simulation that scales from a short rehearsal through a three-quarter and a full-distance simulation to a final race-day test.
prerequisites: Comfortable running continuously for at least twenty minutes
Known one-repetition maximums for Back Squat and Deadlift
Basic technique on sled push/pull and wall ball
warnings: The weekly simulation session is performed as one ordered pass through every station with no automatic rest between them -- pace accordingly.
Compromised running (Day 4) is deliberately fatiguing; stop a run leg early if form breaks down.
Percentages and distances are prescriptions, not automatic readiness or safety decisions.

provenance.statement: GymTracker authored every weekly distance, load, repetition, and station in this eight-week adaptation. Public endurance and hybrid-fitness training literature supports only the general base-build-peak-taper shape and the principle of race-pace simulation before a target event, not this program's specific numbers. This is not presented as any race organizer's, gym's, or coach's official program.

programDefinitions.name: Multi-Erg Interval Rotation
programDefinitions.description: A four-week original GymTracker rotation across SkiErg, RowErg, and BikeErg. Session A repeats a four-minute-per-machine rotation for two or three rounds; Session B is a fixed five-segment pyramid across the same three machines. Both sessions shorten their recovery and Session A adds a round as the weeks progress.
warnings: Schedule the two sessions on non-consecutive days.
Pace every machine interval evenly rather than starting each one all-out.

provenance.statement: GymTracker authored every interval length, round count, rest period, and machine order in this four-week rotation. Public conditioning literature supports only the general principle of multi-modal ergometer intervals with progressively shorter recovery, not this program's specific schedule. This is not presented as any manufacturer's or coach's official program.
